name: Imperial Capitals
sourceNote: Brush-drawn Trajan capitals after David Harris, The Art of Calligraphy, pp. 113-119 (Catich's tradition). Flat brush, cap height 8 brush widths.
moves: twist the brush from 30 to 90 degrees
turn the brush over and twist from 150 to 90 degrees

strokes.move: top arm: twist the brush from 30 to 90 degrees to create the top serif
bowl curving back to the stem
foot: turn the brush over and twist from 150 to 90 degrees
foot of the L (the E's foot, longer): turn the brush over and twist from 150 to 90 degrees
crossbar drawn at 30 degrees, joining two I's
tail of the R: flatten the brush to the horizontal before edging off
top serif: twist the brush from 30 to 90 degrees
bottom serif: turn the brush over and twist from 150 degrees
top serif of the stem: pull horizontally, then twist 30 to 90
tail of the Q: sweeps well below the baseline, breaking the bilinear form; slightly turn the brush to horizontal before edging off
pull to the right before commencing the arc
joining stroke, always above the stem's centre
lower bowl, one sweep, with the fillet at the stem's foot
left leg (always thinner than the right)
right foot serif: edge off with the tip of the brush
the apex must be drawn first
draw the apex of the letter first
the diagonal is the thickest of the three strokes
arm, like the right fork of the V
leg: turn the brush to the horizontal before edging off
tail sweeping out to the left
tail serif, drawn second, while the hand remembers (tip first)
cross stroke first: edge twisting back to 30, finishing at 90 degrees
bottom curve sweeping up to meet the right stem
first stroke: begins as a vertical, finishes at the apex
second stroke: slightly twist the brush to finish at its angle
down diagonal (top v smaller than the bottom)
cross diagonal; no serif on the right inner leg
top arm: twist the brush to 30 degrees and move horizontally
diagonal: brush held near the horizontal to create a thick diagonal
bottom arm: turn the brush over and twist from 150 to 90 degrees
